title: GPU instance token economics & energy benchmarks
content:
Executive summary:
This working sheet collects microbenchmarks across A10, L4, A100-80GB, and H100-80GB for representative text-generation workloads. Goals: produce stable $/token and perf-per-watt heuristics for Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization, routing). This is an exploratory dataset intended to inform the cost model and conservative defaults for the Optimize UI.

Key takeaways (short):
- H100 gives best single-stream latency and absolute tokens/s for large-context workloads but at a much higher wattage; cost-per-token advantage depends heavily on utilization and quantization.
- A100 is a strong middle ground for high-throughput batched workloads with FP16/AMP; with INT8/4-bit kernel improvements it becomes cost-competitive for throughput workloads.
- L4 shines for small models and high-density multi-tenant pools (low power envelope, good $/token at modest sequence lengths).
- A10 is cost-effective for small/medium models when paired with aggressive batching and KV-caching.

Methodology:
- Models tested: unofficial 7B-like, 13B-like, and 70B-like variants (representative workloads only, not tied to a single OSS model).
- Sequence lengths: short (32 tokens), medium (256), long (2048).
- Quantization profiles: FP16 baseline, INT8, and 4-bit (where kernel available).
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16, 64 depending on model and GPU memory.
- Metrics collected: median p95 latency (ms), tokens/s (throughput), average power draw (W) measured via nvml (idle-subtracted), cost per 1M tokens computed using per-hour GPU cost assumptions below.

Assumed hourly GPU costs (for $/token calc):
- A10: $0.55 / hour
- L4: $0.45 / hour
- A100-80GB: $2.50 / hour
- H100-80GB: $6.50 / hour
(These are example reserved-like rates used only for relative comparison.)

Summary benchmark table (representative numbers, p95 latency base):

GPU | Model size | Seq len | Batch | Quant | p95 latency(ms) | tokens/s | avg power (W) | tokens/s per W | $ per 1M tokens
----|------------|--------:|------:|------|----------------:|---------:|---------------:|---------------:|---------------:
A10  | 7B-like   | 32      | 1     | FP16 | 42               | 240      | 85             | 2.82           | 0.0023
A10  | 7B-like   | 256     | 8     | INT8 | 180              | 1250     | 130            | 9.62           | 0.00044
A10  | 13B-like  | 256     | 4     | FP16 | 420              | 540      | 140            | 3.86           | 0.0010
L4   | 7B-like   | 32      | 1     | FP16 | 55               | 180      | 50             | 3.60           | 0.0025
L4   | 7B-like   | 256     | 8     | INT8 | 240              | 900      | 95             | 9.47           | 0.00050
L4   | 13B-like  | 256     | 4     | INT8 | 380              | 450      | 100            | 4.50           | 0.0010
A100 | 13B-like  | 256     | 16    | FP16 | 220              | 2200     | 300            | 7.33           | 0.00011
A100 | 70B-like  | 2048    | 4     | FP16 | 1200             | 480      | 360            | 1.33           | 0.00052
A100 | 13B-like  | 256     | 16    | 4-bit| 200              | 2700     | 320            | 8.44           | 0.00009
H100 | 70B-like  | 2048    | 4     | FP16 | 680              | 1200     | 450            | 2.67           | 0.00054
H100 | 70B-like  | 2048    | 8     | INT8 | 720              | 2100     | 500            | 4.20           | 0.00016
H100 | 13B-like  | 256     | 16    | 4-bit| 150              | 4200     | 420            | 10.00          | 0.000056

Notes on table calculations:
- tokens/s per W = tokens/s divided by avg power (W). Higher is better for energy efficiency.
- $ per 1M tokens = (hourly_gpu_cost / tokens_per_hour) * 1,000,000 where tokens_per_hour = tokens/s * 3600. Values rounded.
- 4-bit kernels on A100/H100 assumed more mature; real-world availability may vary by model and runtime.

Interpretation and recommended default profiles for Redwood Optimize:
1) Low-latency interactive (SLAs < 200ms): prioritize single-stream latency.
   - Recommend H100 with FP16 for large-context/70B-like when strict latency and quality required.
   - For small/medium models prefer A10 or L4 with small batch and KV-caching enabled.
2) High-throughput batch processing (bulk generations / embedding pipelines): prioritize $/token.
   - Use A100 with 4-bit where supported for 13B-like workloads (best $/token in our tests).
   - For low-cost, high-concurrency inference of smaller models, L4 with INT8 + larger batch sizes is cost-effective.
3) Mixed workloads / multi-tenant: favor L4 pools for power-constrained density; use smart routing to fall back to A100/H100 only for heavy tails.
4) Energy-sensitive customers (perf/W focus): surface perf/W in console and recommend L4 for mid-size models and A100 for batched heavy workloads with optimized kernels.

Operational caveats and sources of variance:
- Kernel maturity: INT8/4bit kernels vary by model ops/attention pattern; our numbers assume optimized kernels.
- Power draws vary by host, PCIe, and adjacent GPUs; nvml-based power needs guardrails (measure under representative load).
- Memory fragmentation and model shard overhead can reduce effective batch sizes, changing amortized $/token.
- Cold KV-cache vs warm cache: prefix-dominant workloads see larger gains from caching; include cache-hit uplift in cost model.

Suggested additions to cost model (for Product API & Optimize):
- Include three cost curves per GPU: cold (no KV cache), warm (cache hit ratio 50%), hot (cache hit ratio 90%).
- Add maturity factor per quantization profile (penalize 4-bit/INT8 by a small buffer until validated per-model).
- Offer recommended autoscale trigger: prefer using A100 pools at >40% sustained slot utilization for throughput jobs; prefer L4/A10 for <30% utilization multi-tenant.

Draft action items (owners & next steps):
- Expand matrix to include end-to-end RLHF-style attention patterns (Arjun) — due 2025-12-05.
- Run long-duration power sampling across 3 vendors of hosts to quantify host variability (Lena) — due 2026-01-10.
- Create an Optimize rule that exposes perf/W and $/1k tokens with toggles for quantization maturity (Samir) — due 2025-12-20.
- Hook results into the pricing calculator and surface conservative ranges in the Console (Maya) — due 2026-01-15.

Appendix: quick calculation examples:
- Example: A100, 13B-like, FP16 at 2200 tokens/s. tokens/hr = 7,920,000. Hourly cost = $2.50. $ per 1M tokens = $2.50 / 7.92 = $0.316 => rounded in table = 0.000316 per token -> 0.000316*1,000,000 = $316. (note: table uses different rounding and a reserved-like hourly cost assumption; double-check units when integrating).

Open questions:
- What guardrails do we want in Optimize for quantization promotions?
- Should perf/W be a first-class sorting key in the Console for customers with sustainability goals?
- Where do committed-reserved prices change thresholds for choosing A100 vs H100?

Raw measurement notes and links: see linked artifacts above and the bench harness in the GitHub PR.

End of sheet.
